newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - T-bonds face correction, aim for 110-31.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-bonds face correction, aim for 110-31.

text.p: September T-bonds are set for a classic period of consolidation to the end of the month and could trade down around a point before resuming their bull trend, technical analysts said on Thursday.
"We're seeing a classic bit of technical price action -- a correction in an otherwise bull market," said Bill Westgate, vice president at HSBC Securities in London.

He said a dearth of data as the month-end approaches and the fact that T-bonds were trading at the very top of a steep upchannel, meant the market was primed for a small sell-off, before pushing higher again.

"There is a clear upchannel with a bottom around 110-00 and a top around 113-00," said Westgate. "We could probably trade down another point or so, but any lower prices should be seen as a buying opportunity before moving higher."
Wednesday's $11.5 billion five year note auction, plus the $2.8 billion multi-tranche global issue announced by New Jersey, helped to tip the market into correction mode, Westgate said.
Analysts at MCM YieldWatch here agreed setbacks were likely within a medium term bull trend.
"The loss of 111-17 yesterday opens a setback to 110-31 initially, with daily studies and candles now firmly in bear correction mode," they said in a note for clients.
The 110-31 level is a 38 percent retracement of the rally from 108-05 on May 27 to 112-24 on June 20.
By 0910 GMT, September T-bonds were down 2/32 at 111-21. December eurodollars were up 0.005 at 93.950.
One analyst said with Stochastics rolling over to give a fresh sell signal, the correction in eurodollars could be extended towards main support at 93.805.
